subject.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser

question: Should the embedded LSP runtime enforce a universal 10 MB response-frame ceiling, or use another evidence-backed limit policy?
rationale: The protocol does not define this ceiling, and imposing it can terminate existing language-server sessions that current OpenClaw accepts, so the permanent compatibility policy requires owner intent.

options.title: Choose an evidence-backed limit
options.body: Measure or document supported-server response behavior and retain a finite owner-approved bound with upgrade and real-subprocess proof.

options.title: Keep 10 MB explicitly
options.body: Retain the proposed ceiling only after the relevant owner confirms that larger supported responses are not required and accepts the compatibility impact.

options.title: Harden unsafe lengths only
options.body: Land non-safe-integer rejection separately and defer finite-size policy until its compatibility contract is established.

recommendation.title: Choose an evidence-backed limit
recommendation.body: Measure or document supported-server response behavior and retain a finite owner-approved bound with upgrade and real-subprocess proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current embedded LSP runtime and its session lifecycle on main.
